    Import tracks from OpenStreetMap

    OpenStreetMap knows most karting tracks in the world (name, position, often the website). Pick a country, tick the tracks worth having, import — they become catalogue pages that drivers find by GPS when they upload.

    Layouts

    Layout

    Shown on the track page and in the upload window so drivers pick the right configuration.
    Open layout page

    1Track line

    2Corner numbering

    Corners are found automatically from the radius threshold. With “Edit corners” on, click the line to add a corner, right-click a number to remove it.

    3Satellite imagery

    GPS and imagery can be a few metres apart. With “Align imagery” on, drag the picture under the line (or use the arrows, 0.5 m a step) until the track matches, then save.

    How to get the file out of an Alfano

    From the lap timer

    Put the lap timer in Bluetooth mode: Alfano 7 — turn Bluetooth on in its menu (the green light comes on); RaceBox — just turn it on.

    This browser has no Bluetooth — use the Hutka app, or Chrome on Android or a computer.
    Nearby devices
    No lap timer yet…

    Hutka does not speak this device's language yet. Everything it says is recorded here: put it in Bluetooth mode, press its buttons, start a transfer in its menu — then send the log. That is how the download gets written.

    The browser cannot open this device's services, so Hutka cannot read it over Bluetooth here. Upload the session file instead — for an AiM MyChron, the .xrk file Race Studio 3 downloads from it.
